mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day rolling mean during the high-rate period (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which anticipates higher corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE divergence and SPX 20-day returns is < 0.2 (Spearman's rho).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests expanding economic demand, which elevates investor confidence and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 50 instances, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when INDPRO growth is above 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in the GDP deflator (not directly observable here; therefore this sketch is invalid per the rules) — instead, use a supply proxy: A prolonged decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three months reduces expectations of rate hikes, supporting positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During the CPIAUCSL < 3% regime, 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day moving average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of RSAFS to GDPC1 exceeds 0.8 for two consecutive months, it indicates a shift toward credit-driven demand, which often precedes a rate cut and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Over 10 such triggers, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% followed by a sustained rise in labor participation (PAYEMS) suggests a labor market recovery that boosts earnings and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% and PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During the defined trigger, SPX 20-day returns show no significant correlation with the UNRATE/PAYEMS pattern (Spearman < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) combined with weak industrial production (INDPRO) indicates supply-side softness that can lead to risk aversion and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: Over 40 instances of CPIAUCSL < previous month and INDPRO < previous month, the 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate remains below 4% for three consecutive months during a regime of falling inflation (CPIAUCSL), it suggests the FOMC is likely to hold rates steady, which supports positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 3% for two months and FEDFUNDS < 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day rolling mean (p > 0.05).
